subject: Request: latest penetration test report for Hosted API and secure transfer
messages:
From: Jamie Simms <jamie.simms@maplecloud.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: Alex Tsu <alex.tsu@maplecloud.com>
Date: 2026-08-22T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Quick request — latest pentest for Hosted API and sharing method

Hi Grace / Monica,

Hope you’re well. MapleCloud is updating our vendor risk file and we need the most recent penetration test covering Redwood’s Hosted API. Two quick asks: 1) Can you confirm the scope (production vs. staging) for the latest report? 2) What secure sharing methods do you support — we prefer ephemeral links for full reports, or an SFTP drop with key rotation.

Also, if there are any redacted findings or an executive summary we can initially share, that would speed our intake. We’ll also need a point of contact for remediation status follow-ups.

Thanks — appreciate a quick turnaround if possible.

—Jamie
Jamie Simms
Security Operations Manager
MapleCloud Health
jamie.simms@maplecloud.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: Jamie Simms <jamie.simms@maplecloud.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-22T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick request — latest pentest for Hosted API and sharing method

Hi Jamie — thanks for the note. I can help get this over. Quick answers up front:
- Scope: the latest full pentest covers our Hosted API production endpoints (v2) and the public control plane — not customer-managed private deployments.
- Sharing options: we support an encrypted artifact via our Evidence Portal (ephemeral, time-limited link), and can also provide an SFTP transfer with rotating keys. We strongly prefer the portal for full reports because it supports download auditing.

Couple clarifying Qs before I pull the full report:
1) Do you need the unredacted findings or is a redacted version + executive summary sufficient for your GRC intake?
2) Any contractual NDAs or additional sign-off required on your side? (We can route via DocuSign for a short non-disclosure addendum if needed.)

Timeline: if you confirm you can accept an ephemeral portal link and a standard redaction (IP and customer identifiers), I can have an executive summary today and an encrypted full package by EOD tomorrow.

If that works I’ll loop in our security team to prepare the package and a short remediation status snapshot.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.ai

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai

Date: 2026-08-22T10:15:00-07:00

Forwarding request from MapleCloud (security ops). They want the latest Hosted API pentest and prefer ephemeral links; they also asked about scope and redaction.

Key asks for you:
- Confirm the most recent pentest artifact we can share for production-hosted API (report version and date).
- Recommend redaction policy (we usually remove customer identifiers + limited IP details).
- Prepare an encrypted bundle with checksum and advise on password SOP (portal vs. zip password).

Jamie indicated they'd accept a redacted report + exec summary to get through intake quickly. If security signs off, I’ll send the portal link and a short DocuSign NDA for their legal.

Thanks — please reply with the artifact name and any objections.

—Grace

Thanks for the heads-up. Quick notes from Security:
- Artifact: the most recent eligible artifact is "redwood_pt_summary_v3.pdf" (exec summary, redacted) and the full report bundle is "redwood_pt_encrypted_20260824.zip" (AES-256, password-protected). The full assessment targets production Hosted API v2 and control plane, test window June 12–18, 2026.
- Redaction: we will remove customer identifiers and internal IP ranges; we will not redact technical findings that are necessary for remediation context.
- Sharing method: Evidence Portal ephemeral links are preferred because they provide audit logs and expire by default after 72 hours. For SFTP we can support a 24-hour key rotation window, but it requires manual provisioning.
- Password handling: Portal will host the artifact and we’ll send the password to your security point via a separate channel (SMS or an alternate email). If they prefer a zipped artifact, we’ll encrypt and share the password over DocuSign or via a phone call to an authorized contact.

No objections to sharing a redacted executive summary today and the full encrypted bundle tomorrow.

Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Security Operations | Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai

1) Executive summary (redwood_pt_summary_v3.pdf) — attached to this message for immediate intake. This file redacts customer identifiers and internal IP ranges.

2) Full encrypted report package — available via our Evidence Portal: https://evidence.redwood.ai/portal/ephemeral/abcdef123 (expires in 72 hours). Artifact name: redwood_pt_encrypted_20260824.zip. The portal includes download auditing.

3) Password & verification — we’ve initiated a short DocuSign verification that an authorized MapleCloud security contact signs. Once signed, we will push the password to the designated contact via SMS and post a one-time code in the portal metadata. Link: https://www.docusign.com/IN/123456789

If you prefer direct SFTP instead, we can provision a temporary account with a 24-hour rotating key; let me know and I’ll ask Ops to provision immediately.

Timeline for remediation updates: our security team will provide a short remediation status snapshot (open findings affecting Hosted API) within three business days and can set up a 30-minute sync if you want to walk through any items.

Next steps for you: please sign the DocuSign verification or confirm you want the SFTP option and we’ll proceed.

Best,
